name: std::is_corresponding_member

declarations.code:
template <class S1, class S2, class M1, class M2>

constexpr bool is_corresponding_member(M1 S1::*mp, M2 S2::*mq) noexcept;

intro:
Determines whether mp and mq refer corresponding members in the common initial sequence of S1 and S2. The program is ill-formed if either S1 or S2 is an incomplete type.

If either S1 or S2 is not a StandardLayoutType, or either M1 or M2 is not an object type, or either mp or mq is equal to nullptr, the result is always false.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: true if mp and mq refer corresponding members in the common initial sequence of S1 and S2, otherwise false.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: The type of a pointer-to-member expression &S::m is not always M S::*, where m is of type M, because m may be a member inherited from a base class of S. The template arguments can be specified in order to avoid potentially surprising results.
